title: Viva Engage: handle GDPR deletion requests in the Engage admin center
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents Graph automation for assigning Verified and Network administrator roles, but the briefing says neither role has documented automation. The default-on assertion and cost classification also need correction, and the REST permission note omits the reference's paid-network qualification.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes managing GDPR deletion requests directly within the Engage admin center.
claims.quote: You can now manage GDPR deletion requests directly within the Engage admin center, streamlining the process and reducing reliance on the legacy Yammer admin center. This update centralizes compliance actions in one modern interface.

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified at 2025-06-05T23:00:34.
The GDPR removal options are at Viva Engage admin center > Governance and compliance > Data management > Manage GDPR data subject requests > removal option.
claims.quote: Select Governance and compliance > Data management. Check the options for Manage GDPR data subject requests. GDPR subject requests support three distinct options:

claims.claim: DELETE https://www.yammer.com/api/v1/users/:user_id.json?gdpr_delete=true submits a GDPR deletion request.
claims.quote: https://www.yammer.com/api/v1/users/:user_id.json; gdpr_delete=true — submits a GDPR deletion request. Asynchronously erases the user’s PII across systems and anonymizes authored content (messages remain but are no longer attributable).

claims.claim: A tenant role assignment can be made at Microsoft Entra admin center > Identity > Roles & admins > role > Add assignments.
claims.quote: Browse to Identity > Roles & admins. Select a role name to open the role. Don't add a check mark next to the role. Select Add assignments and then select the users, groups, or agent identities you want to assign to this role.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments creates a Microsoft Entra directory role assignment.
claims.quote: Create a new unifiedRoleAssignment object. POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments

claims.claim: The Verified Admin assignment route is Yammer admin center > Admins > Current Admins > user > Grant Verified Admin.
claims.quote: If the user is already an admin, find their name from the Current Admins list and select Grant Verified Admin.
claims.fix: Keep the path, but add 'This Current Admins route is for a user who is already an admin' to controls[2].note and the rendered note. The cited roles page gives a different initial step for a non-admin.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation for assigning the Viva Engage Verified Admin role.
claims.quote: Viva Engage supports role-based access by enabling the assignment of predefined administrative roles (such as Network Administrator and Verified Administrator) ... Assign a Viva Engage role to a user: POST /employeeExperience/roles/{engagementRoleId}/members.
claims.fix: Set controls[2].api to kind 'graph', call 'POST /v1.0/employeeExperience/roles/{engagementRoleId}/members', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/engagementrole-post-members?view=graph-rest-1.0'. Add to its note: 'For native-mode networks, use the Verified Administrator engagementRoleId; the request identifies the assignee through user@odata.bind. Requires EngagementRole.ReadWrite.All.' Update the rendered API cell and cite the operation reference and https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/engagement-api-overview?view=graph-rest-1.0.

claims.claim: The Network Admin assignment route is Yammer admin center > Admins > Current Admins > user > Grant Network Admin.
claims.quote: If the user is already an admin, find their name from the Current Admins list and select Grant Network Admin.
claims.fix: Keep the path, but add 'This Current Admins route is for a user who is already an admin' to controls[3].note and the rendered note. The cited roles page gives a different initial step for a non-admin.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation for assigning the Viva Engage Network Admin role.
claims.quote: Viva Engage supports role-based access by enabling the assignment of predefined administrative roles (such as Network Administrator and Verified Administrator) ... Assign a Viva Engage role to a user: POST /employeeExperience/roles/{engagementRoleId}/members.
claims.fix: Set controls[3].api to kind 'graph', call 'POST /v1.0/employeeExperience/roles/{engagementRoleId}/members', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/engagementrole-post-members?view=graph-rest-1.0'. claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The module is on by default on arrival, without an administrator taking action.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Viva Engage Manage GDPR data subject requests module enable disable license price meter'; read the roadmap, Manage GDPR data subject requests for Viva Engage users, and Overview of the Viva Engage admin center. Availability is stated, but automatic rollout/default state is not.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to 'unknown'. Replace 'If nobody acts, the module is there for those roles to use' with 'Microsoft documents access for these roles but does not state the module's default or rollout mechanics.' Do not infer the default from the absence of an enablement step.

claims.claim: The module offers three GDPR deletion options.
claims.quote: GDPR subject requests support three distinct options:

claims.claim: Permanently remove this user, but retain their messages removes the user while retaining their messages and content.
claims.quote: Permanently remove this user, but retain their messages - Removes the user and retains their posted messages and content.

claims.claim: Permanently remove this user, and remove their messages removes the user and their posted messages and content.
claims.quote: Permanently remove this user, and remove their messages - Removes the user and their posted messages and content.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Removing the user and their messages is irreversible.
claims.quote: Permanently remove this user, and remove their messages - Removes the user and their posted messages and content. You can't reverse this action.

claims.claim: Erase this user wipes the user's personal information.
claims.quote: Erase this user. Wipe their name and personal information, but leave their messages (Can't be undone after 14 days)

claims.claim: Erasing the user leaves their messages and files in place.
claims.quote: When you erase a user, the action removes their personally identifying information, but their messages and files remain.

claims.claim: Erase this user deactivates the user for 14 days before permanent deletion so administrators can evaluate files and messages.
claims.quote: Deactivates the user for 14 days to give the admin time to evaluate files and messages before permanently deleting the user.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Erase this user cannot be undone after 14 days.
claims.quote: Erase this user. Wipe their name and personal information, but leave their messages (Can't be undone after 14 days)

claims.claim: The administrator confirms the selected removal option with Remove user.
claims.quote: When finished, select Remove user.

claims.claim: All three deletion options remove follows and follower connections.
claims.quote: All choices for deletion remove the following data: Who the user follows, what conversations and articles they follow, and who follows them

claims.claim: All three deletion options remove bookmarks.
claims.quote: All choices for deletion remove the following data: ... The user's bookmarks, language preferences, notification settings, and account activity

claims.claim: All three deletion options remove the user's language and notification settings.
claims.quote: All choices for deletion remove the following data: ... The user's bookmarks, language preferences, notification settings, and account activity

claims.claim: All three deletion options remove account activity.
claims.quote: All choices for deletion remove the following data: ... The user's bookmarks, language preferences, notification settings, and account activity

claims.claim: All three deletion options remove the user profile.
claims.quote: All choices for deletion remove the following data: ... The user profile

claims.claim: All three deletion options remove group memberships.
claims.quote: All choices for deletion remove the following data: ... The user's group memberships

claims.claim: All three deletion options remove the user's org chart data.
claims.quote: All choices for deletion remove the following data: ... Org chart

claims.claim: All three deletion options remove the user's network list.
claims.quote: All choices for deletion remove the following data: ... The list of networks for which they were a member.

claims.claim: The first two deletion options preserve the user's name in stored Viva Engage data.
claims.quote: The first two deletion options preserve the user's name in Viva Engage's stored data.

claims.claim: Erase this user additionally removes the user's name from stored Viva Engage data.
claims.quote: The Erase this user option also removes the user's name.

claims.claim: The module's Learn page lists no step to switch the module on.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Viva Engage Manage GDPR data subject requests module enable disable license price meter'; read the module page in full. Its sequence is admin center, Governance and compliance > Data management, removal options, Remove user; no switch-on step is listed.

claims.claim: Data subject requests carry deadlines.
claims.quote: Record the date and time of the request. (You have one month to complete the request.)

claims.claim: Closing a Microsoft Entra ID account does not delete the user's Engage information.
claims.quote: Closing a Microsoft Entra ID account doesn't delete the user and their information. To delete user information, go to the Viva Engage admin center and complete the following instructions.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: After the 14-day erase window, administrators cannot associate the remaining content with the user for export, review and deletion.
claims.quote: After the user account transitions from Deactivated to Removed, you can't associate user data with that user, which means you can't export and review their data.

claims.claim: After 14 days, retained messages and files are marked as belonging to a former user.
claims.quote: After the 14-day window, files and messages remain, but are marked as belonging to a former user.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: SharePoint-stored Engage files must be deleted from Viva Engage to remove both the file and Viva Engage metadata.
claims.quote: For Viva Engage files stored in SharePoint, delete the files from Viva Engage in order to remove the Viva Engage metadata and the file.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Erase User in Viva Engage does not delete the user's Office 365 or Microsoft Entra profile.
claims.quote: The Erase User option deletes the user's Viva Engage profile, but doesn't delete their Office 365 or Microsoft Entra profile.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The documented module procedure acts through an administrator selecting a removal option and Remove user.
claims.quote: Check the options for Manage GDPR data subject requests. GDPR subject requests support three distinct options: ... When finished, select Remove user.

claims.claim: Removing a user from their home Viva Engage tenant removes them from all external tenants.
claims.quote: Removing a user from their home Viva Engage tenant removes them from all external tenants.

claims.claim: Guests must be removed separately from each external tenant.
claims.quote: You must separately remove guests from each of their external tenants.

claims.where: Scope; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: For reviewing which files and messages to keep or delete, Microsoft's guidance starts with a home-tenant per-user export before erasing.
claims.quote: Review files and messages created by the user and decide which to keep and which to delete: 1. Do one per-user export of the user's data for the home tenant ... 2. In the home tenant, use the Erase this user option.

claims.claim: The review workflow also calls for a per-user export for each external tenant, if any.
claims.quote: Do one per-user export of the user's data for the home tenant, and one for each external tenant if any.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft's GDPR guidance instructs administrators to choose the approach for their case and follow its steps in order.
claims.quote: Choose the approach that applies for your case, and follow the steps in the order listed. The order matters: after you erase a user, you can't find their data to delete it.

claims.claim: Engage Administrator is also called Yammer administrator in Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: This role is also referred to as Yammer administrator in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The Engage Administrator role is assigned in Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: Assign the Engage admin role in Microsoft Entra ID or Privileged Identity Management (PIM).

claims.claim: At least Privileged Role Administrator is required to assign tenant roles as a signed-in administrator.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least a Privileged Role Administrator.

claims.claim: The directory role assignment body sets roleDefinitionId to identify the assigned role.
claims.quote: roleDefinitionId: Identifier of the unifiedRoleDefinition the assignment is for. ... roleDefinitionId can be either the service-wide template Id or the directory-specific roleDefinitionId.

claims.claim: The directory role assignment body sets principalId to identify the assignee.
claims.quote: principalId | String | Required. Identifier of the principal to which the assignment is granted.

claims.claim: The directory role assignment body uses directoryScopeId with / for tenant-wide scope.
claims.quote: For the directory (Microsoft Entra ID) provider, this property supports the following formats: - / for tenant-wide scope

claims.claim: An Engage admin or verified admin can assign Verified Administrator.
claims.quote: Verified Administrator: Who can assign | Engage admin or verified admin

claims.claim: Engage admins, network admins and verified admins can assign Network Administrator.
claims.quote: Network Administrator: Who can assign | Engage admin or network admin and verified admin

claims.claim: The Yammer Data Export API reads the admin list rather than assigning administrator roles.
claims.quote: Yammer Data Export API can be used to export admins.csv to read the list of admins

claims.claim: The gdpr_delete=true query parameter selects the GDPR deletion workflow.
claims.quote: gdpr_delete | Query | No | boolean | If true, triggers the GDPR user deletion workflow.

claims.claim: The REST deletion caller must be an admin or verified admin, without a network qualification.
claims.quote: 403 Forbidden | The authenticated caller does not have permission to delete the user (must be an admin, or a verified admin in a paid network).
claims.fix: Replace the caller clause in controls[0].note and the rendered note with 'The reference's response table requires an admin, or a verified admin in a paid network; its introductory text says admin or verified admin in a Viva Engage network.' Use the same qualified wording in the Governance controls paragraph.

claims.claim: The REST GDPR deletion request is irreversible.
claims.quote: Both delete=true and gdpr_delete=true are irreversible and cannot be undone by the user, an admin, or Microsoft Support.

claims.claim: Microsoft cautions against routine API-based lifecycle deletions because of unrecoverable data loss.
claims.quote: User lifecycle management should generally be performed through the Microsoft 365 Admin Center or Microsoft Entra. API-based user deletions may lead to unrecoverable data loss and are therefore not recommended.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Erase User sends a notification to the Viva Engage Inbox of network and verified admins.
claims.quote: When you delete a user by using the Erase User option, the Viva Engage Inbox of all network admins and verified admins receives a notification.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The GDPR guidance specifically says Verified admins can erase users, whereas the module page lists Network, Verified and Engage admins.
claims.quote: Verified admins can erase users from Engage to comply with General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) data subject requests.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The governance checklist's per-user export operation has no corresponding control row.
claims.quote: Run the per-user export for the home tenant and each external tenant before selecting any removal option. The controls table covers user removal and three administrator role assignments, not exports.
claims.fix: The 'Run the per-user export for the home tenant and each external tenant' checklist step has no controls-table row. Remove that checklist bullet while retaining the already documented export prerequisite in Scope; this correction does not add a control row.
